blocks.content: Under individual selection with unrelated group members, there is no contribution from $ \sigma^{2}(A_{s}) $ to the response, and changes in $ A_{s} $ only enter as a correlated response to changes in $ A_{d} $ which can be in an unfavorable direction when $ \sigma(A_{d},A_{s})<0 $ . As we will see, $ \sigma^{2}(A_{s}) $ enters into the response under group selection even when there are no relatives in the group. The reason is that the group phenotype is a function of the distribution of $ A_{s} $ values.

Under strict group selection, selection is based on the group mean, $ $, or equivalently the total value of the group, $ n = z $, and we will usually work with the latter.
